hypothesis: The first keel left the inverted basin but its two segments overlapped by 4–6 mm at the waist and injected forces during ordinary locomotion. Shortening both inner ends to leave a 90 mm surface gap and halving added mass should preserve the rollover support line without cross-waist contact.
expectedEffect: Retain the first keel's lower final inverted tilt and higher torso clearance while eliminating keel-to-keel contact, ordinary-gait regressions, and new disallowed self-collision.
